regime.headline: Risk-on
regime.paragraph: Investors added risk across equities and credit: US Treasury yields 2Y +2bp to 4.70% and 10Y -1bp to 4.99%. The US curve saw a twist flattener in 2s10s (-3bp to 29bp). The dollar rose 0.1%, gold fell 0.2%, the S&P 500 rose 0.6% and Brent fell 2.6%. US high-yield spreads tightened 8bp. The standout move was UK 2Y Gilt (+21bp, 6.3x its 20-day volatility).

regions.name: United States
regions.text: Treasuries were little changed, 2Y +2bp to 4.70% and 10Y -1bp to 4.99%: a twist flattener (2s10s -3bp). Markets added 6bp of Fed tightening over 12 months (now +76bp). The dollar rose 0.1% and the S&P 500 rose 0.6%.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.text: Gilts sold off with the front end leading, 2Y +21bp to 4.94% and 10Y +2bp to 5.35%: a bear flattener (2s10s -19bp). Gilts underperformed Treasuries by 3bp at 10Y. Markets added 3bp of BoE tightening over 12 months (now +116bp). Sterling fell 0.4% and the FTSE 100 fell 0.3%.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Bunds rallied, 2Y -1bp to 3.07% and 10Y -1bp to 3.42%. BTP-Bund was steady 0bp to 107bp. Markets removed 6bp of ECB tightening over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy (now +60bp). The euro fell 0.4% and the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 0.2%.

regions.name: Japan
regions.text: JGB 10Y yields fell 1bp to 2.823%, with 30Y -2bp. The yen weakened as USD/JPY moved +0.2% to 157.82. Markets added 4bp of BoJ tightening over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy (now +122bp). The Nikkei rose 1.1%.

regions.name: China
regions.text: CGB 10Y yields rose 3bp to 1.63%. The renminbi firmed with USD/CNY -0.06% at 6.6659. The CSI 300 rose 0.8% and copper rose 0.3%.

relationships.statement: Lower oil pulled US breakevens down.
relationships.lesson: Energy feeds directly into headline inflation, so short-dated breakevens track oil closely.

relationships.statement: Credit confirmed the equity rally as high-yield spreads tightened.
relationships.lesson: Equities and credit both price corporate risk. When they disagree, credit (the more senior claim) is often the better signal.

relationships.statement: The Treasury curve twisted flatter: tighter policy priced while long-end yields fell on growth risk.
relationships.lesson: Front end sold off while the long end rallied: tighter policy expected, weighing on growth.

relationships.statement: Gilts underperformed Bunds, pointing to UK-specific drivers such as data, BoE pricing or fiscal supply.
relationships.lesson: Cross-market spreads strip out the global rates move, isolating what was local.

interview.question: Why did the UK 10Y outperform the 2Y?
interview.answer: The UK 2Y moved +21bp and the 10Y +2bp, so 2s10s moved -19bp to 41bp: a bear flattener. Front-end yields rose more than the long end: the market is pricing a more hawkish central bank. Market pricing for the BoE over 12 months moved +3bp, which is what drives the front end. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the European Central Bank, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 2.50%. Markets price a 29% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 2.4 hikes (60bp) over 12 months; terminal 3.25%. The 12-month pricing moved -6bp on the day. Method: Government bill-curve proxy (indicative). Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +60bp is 2.4 moves.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Federal Reserve, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 4.00%. Markets price a 10% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 3.0 hikes (76bp) over 12 months; terminal 4.80%. The 12-month pricing moved +6bp on the day. Method: Fed funds futures (CME FedWatch method). Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +76bp is 3.0 moves.

interview.question: How would you characterise today's market regime, and what's your evidence?
interview.answer: Risk-on: investors added risk across equities and credit. The classifier scores each regime's expected cross-asset signature against today's volatility-adjusted moves; the strongest factors were equities. Confidence: medium. In an interview, lead with the conclusion, then two or three confirming moves, then the one asset that does not fit.

interview.question: Why did the US 10Y outperform the 2Y?
interview.answer: The US 2Y moved +2bp and the 10Y -1bp, so 2s10s moved -3bp to 29bp: a twist flattener. Front end sold off while the long end rallied: tighter policy expected, weighing on growth. Market pricing for the Fed over 12 months moved +6bp, which is what drives the front end. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.
